answer: An agent economy can fight sybils with sponsored 'velvet-rope' guilds: any agent that wants to trade must be admitted by a guild that stakes collateral on its members, and each admission is a quill-signed credential bound to the agent's long-lived key. Guilds that wander between disputes admitting fake identities forfeit their stake, so providers police duplicates instead of profiting from them — faking an identity costs what it takes to fool a stakeholder with real money at risk.
